provider: Federal Title & Escrow Company (independent title/settlement company, Chevy Chase MD/DC/VA)
endpoint: ASP.NET WebForms postback (__doPostBack/__VIEWSTATE/__EVENTVALIDATION) driven via plain requests.Session() POSTs, no browser needed. (1) GET Default.aspx, capture hidden fields; (2) POST with __EVENTTARGET=ddlState and ddlState=<Maryland's GUID option value>, plus ddlTransactionType=1 (Purchase), ddlPropertyType=single, ddlPropertyUse=principal, ddlLoanType=1 (Conventional) -- this postback populates ddlCounty, which already defaults to Montgomery selected; (3) final POST with __EVENTTARGET empty, txtPurchasePrice=500000, txtLoanAmount=400000, ddlTranferTaxesPayingBy=Split, rblComplexTransaction=false, rblIsSellerBuilderOrDeveloper=false, and btnGenerateQuote="Get Quote" clicked as a real submit button. No auth, no cookies beyond the session's own ASP.NET_SessionId, no personal data (txtEmailAddress/txtStreetAddress left blank -- confirmed optional, the page's own text states 'No login or personal information required').
scenario: $500,000 purchase price, $400,000 loan, Montgomery County, Maryland (the calculator's own dropdown default for MD -- no substitution needed), residential purchase, Conventional loan, Principal/Owner-Occupied, Transfer/Recordation Tax split 50/50 buyer-seller, not a short sale/REO/new-construction, seller not a builder/developer
methodology: Federal Title's own 'Quick Quote' tool is a classic ASP.NET WebForms app (same postback pattern already proven for FNF/Old Republic/Knight Barry elsewhere in CALCULATORS.md) hosted on the company's own tools.federaltitle.com subdomain -- a genuine first-party calculator, not a third-party platform embed. One EventValidation gotcha encountered and resolved: a 'rblRepeatClient' RadioButtonList (repeat-client question) is rendered on the very first GET but is NOT re-rendered in the response to the state-selection postback -- submitting any value for it on the final POST throws a hard HTTP 500 ('Invalid postback or callback argument', traced to RadioButtonList.LoadPostData), the same 'field for a control not in the current DOM breaks the postback' failure mode already documented for Old Republic's ReoList and Knight Barry's OR county gotchas. Fix: omit rblRepeatClient entirely from the final POST (it is not required once absent from the rendered form). The 24-county MD dropdown (Baltimore City + 23 counties) already defaults to Montgomery County -- Federal Title's own home submarket -- so no county substitution was needed for the standard scenario.
